8.text: As an authorized Staff member, I want trimmed, case-insensitive literal substring search, so that percent and underscore remain ordinary query characters.

9.text: As an authorized Staff member, I want up to 100 Unicode code points of query input and a visible error beyond that limit, so that input is not silently truncated.

10.text: As an authorized Staff member, I want search to reset the result list to its first page while retaining independently authorized selected detail, so that changing a query does not lose my current context.

15.text: As a Staff reviewer, I want pending applications ordered oldest first with 25-row previous/next navigation, so that I can work through the complete permitted queue predictably.

16.text: As a Staff reviewer, I want search, page, selected-person/record and task return state retained in URLs, so that back navigation and task completion restore my place.

17.text: As a Staff reviewer, I want new rows discovered through navigation or explicit refresh, so that background updates do not reorder the task I am reviewing.

18.text: As an authorized audit reader, I want newest-first bounded history and independent detail access, so that all retained permitted history stays reachable without loading it all.

19.text: As an authorized audit reader, I want retained history to remain reachable after eligible account deletion, so that deletion does not erase the existing historical contract.

20.text: As an applicant, I want my inbox paged newest first without Staff-only notes, so that the full permitted history remains private and navigable.

21.text: As an account holder using Home, I want current participation, valid invitations, future Events and visible notices to remain reachable, so that a read budget does not hide permitted work.

22.text: As an account holder using Home, I want the first 25 items per section followed by explicit next-batch loading, so that initial payloads stay bounded while the complete result remains available.

23.text: As a Member, I want all authorized future Events browsable when no day is selected and a selected day filtered server-side, so that the week strip does not impose a hidden time horizon.

25.text: As a Member, I want approved Enrolment, pending/waitlisted Programs, valid invitations and notices to retain their distinct meanings, so that participation is not confused with attendance or approval.

35.text: As an account holder returning after an uncertain response, I want the existing actor/key-bound reconciliation behavior, so that retry or refresh does not duplicate or misattribute an operation.

36.text: As an account holder navigating away from a sensitive workflow, I want dirty-state, frozen-review and late-response disposal behavior preserved, so that stale work cannot overwrite a newer task.

37.text: As an anonymous applicant, I want application creation and device-capability reconciliation to remain separate from signed-in maintenance, so that signup does not unexpectedly create a session or expose credentials.

38.text: As a signed-in applicant, I want correction, withdrawal and resubmission bound to my account and application, so that shared form mechanics cannot merge distinct authority contracts.

39.text: As a Staff decision maker, I want internal notes separated from applicant-visible reasons, so that private review information cannot enter the applicant response.

40.text: As an authorized Staff member changing a restriction, I want Membership status and Security ban actions to remain independent, so that lifting one restriction does not silently change another.

41.text: As an authorized Staff member considering account deletion, I want existing eligibility, last-Admin and retained-history guards enforced by the server, so that presentation changes cannot bypass destructive-action policy.

42.text: As an account holder encountering an unavailable read, I want safe failure without partial private data and an authoritative retry, so that cached state is not mistaken for current permission.

43.text: As an account holder, I want private client reads and reconciliation results to remain transient without automatic retries or persistence, so that sensitive outcomes are not retained or replayed behind my back.

45.text: As a maintainer, I want CVA, Lucide, CSS and Base UI/native HTML to have clear responsibilities, so that variants, icon geometry, theme values and interactions do not acquire duplicate owners.

46.text: As a maintainer, I want official typed form composition, so that field and submission contracts remain understandable without manually mirroring a library's generic signature.

47.text: As a developer adding a business error, I want consistent runtime, RPC and client contracts with native auth kept distinct, so that a valid change does not create contradictory status/code definitions.

48.text: As a developer, I want enforceable runtime/client boundaries that retain legitimate type-only imports and composition roots, so that static restrictions catch meaningful mistakes without banning valid architecture.

49.text: As a developer refactoring UI files, I want mobile coverage to follow capability through creation, rename and extraction, so that a new filename cannot silently remove a required browser engine.

50.text: As a developer using affected or staged qualification, I want unknown paths to fail closed and parent/cumulative bases distinguished, so that an incomplete selection cannot appear green.

51.text: As a maintainer of a mutation, I want command intent clear while ordered batches, immutable history and SQL predicates stay intact, so that readability does not split an atomic operation.

52.text: As an operator rehearsing schema changes, I want fresh and populated disposable D1 upgrades using synthetic data, so that retained rows, counters and search projections are checked without touching personal stores.

53.text: As a reviewer, I want tests at the real HTTP, D1 and browser boundary, so that a mock, screenshot or source check cannot stand in for authorization and persistence evidence.

54.text: As a maintainer of native tooling, I want owned process cleanup characterized after success, failure, interruption and timeout, so that leader exit is not mistaken for descendant absence.

55.text: As a developer building the app, I want production/native style and asset parity checked on one candidate, so that different source discovery policies do not hide a presentation regression.

56.text: As a developer reusing a build, I want cache hits, misses, invalidation, corruption, relocation and unavailable-storage behavior verified, so that only compatible immutable output is reused.

57.text: As an account holder, I want mutable state, credentials, evidence and passing results excluded from build caches, so that build reuse cannot retain private data or replace fresh testing.

58.text: As an operator diagnosing a failure, I want fixed safe stage/category/outcome information, so that the failure is attributable without raw exceptions, credentials, contacts, cookies or SQL bindings.

59.text: As a maintainer using the Design Book locally, I want valid reference paths served while outside and same-prefix sibling paths are rejected, so that the helper honors its intended filesystem boundary.

60.text: As a maintainer, I want Book screens, original references and licenses preserved during retirement, so that useful design authority is not mistaken for dead product code.

61.text: As a reviewer, I want every tracked file to retain a justified disposition at the final candidate, so that untouched or newly extracted files cannot disappear into a catch-all.

62.text: As a maintainer, I want existing guides, glossary and meaningful ADRs updated through their current owners, so that the programme leaves clear instructions without a competing documentation hierarchy.

63.text: As a programme owner, I want all agreed work planned together and reviewed in seven phases, so that phased delivery does not become silent deferral of the remaining work.

64.text: As a programme owner, I want exact-candidate qualification, independent review and owner acceptance recorded separately, so that foundation readiness is not mistaken for approval to merge, deploy or start Roles implementation.
